title: Remix
abstract: Lessig highlights the newest cultural war being waged on those who create and consume art. Arguing that we reject a copyright system that criminalizes the value of protecting art, he offers an inspiring vision of the post-war world where opportunities await those who view art as a resource to be shared openly rather than a commodity to be hoarded.

narrative:
Short impact summary

Remix (2008), published by Bloomsbury Academic, has been cited 1,059 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 1% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it has been downloaded 4,091 times.

Full narrative

Remix by Lawrence Lessig was published by Bloomsbury Academic in 2008. Conceptually, the work connects to Computer science.

OpenAlex records 1,059 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2019 with 120 citing works. Notable citing venues include Cambridge University Press eBooks, SSRN Electronic Journal and Sustainability. The citing works include 540 journal articles, 301 book chapters and 47 preprints. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia.

It has been downloaded 4,091 times via OAPEN. Open Library reports a combined count of 8 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Peace, Justice and strong institutions among the Sustainable Development Goals.

The latest English Wikipedia check verified 11 article–work reference matches. These are references or bibliography entries, which may include other editions of the same work; they do not measure readership.
